title: Founder-Market Fit
equation: Founder-Market Fit = (Lived Experience + Identity Alignment + Mission Conviction) ÷ 3
hook: A perfect resume doesn't mean you understand your customer. Living their problem does.
statement: Founders win when their life experience, identity, and obsessions line up with the market they serve.
explainer: If you've lived the customer's problem, you learn faster, hire better, and tell a truer story. Smart outsiders often build plans that look right and still miss what customers want.
sop: Write why this market is yours specifically to serve.
Name the lived experience that gives you an unfair insight.
Check that insight against current customers.
Use it in your storytelling and hiring.
Rethink the market if the connection turns out shallow.
equation_example: Score each 1 to 10. Lived Experience 9, Identity Alignment 7, Mission Conviction 8. (9 + 7 + 8) ÷ 3 = 8.0. Higher means you get the customer in your gut. Lower means your plan might look smart and still miss.
question: Write one sentence on why you're the right person for this market, specific enough that nobody else could say it.
closing_statement: Unfair advantage comes from lived experience, not resumes.
caption:
Principle Nº 308: Founder-Market Fit

A perfect resume doesn't mean you understand your customer. Living their problem does.

Founders win when their life experience, identity, and obsessions line up with the market they serve.

Your turn: Write one sentence on why you're the right person for this market, specific enough that nobody else could say it.
